title: Carry familiar acceleration and knee strength forward
stage_label: Main-program exemplar · individually authored · written athletic design reviewed
status_note: The written athletic prescription has passed its scoped design and numeric review using inspected local candidates. Current canonical release, actual inventory/geometry and a precise separate tumbling session are unverified. No athlete history or operational approval is fabricated.
brief: Retain the established short acceleration and productive knee-pattern work, with a brief comparable observation inside normal training. Acceleration leads while fresh; full-body strength develops/retains useful force, and the small brace role preserves control without another fatigue circuit. No beginner month or novelty is added.
quality_target: Repeat the qualified start, run through the endpoint and use the runoff under control. Complete the selected strength doses at owned range with the intended reserve; identify any changed readiness before altering a later prescription. No promised speed gain or maximum strength test.
continuity: Latest relevant productive AND lighter/review records from the prior block →Day1's exact selected age/readiness dose →Day10 comparable ACC focus. Day2 JUMP is adjacent and may require L; all individual anchor links are separately recorded. Actual prior/finished work remains unknown until supplied.
audience: 15 continuing athletes, ages12–14 as reference, with explicit9–11 and15–18 prescriptions. Planning assumption: the selected static start, goblet, hinge and upper-body variations are already familiar/qualified at compatible doses. A birthday does not establish experience. Compare actual history before delivery; exact deviations are recorded, never inferred as completed work. If actual prior distance, tempo or variation differs, preserve a feasible qualified established prescription or record the justified change/new comparison and recalculate before delivery; do not silently rewrite that history to match this reference.
readiness: Check pain/restrictions, sleep/readiness, recent sport/tumbling/other lifting and upcoming commitments. D requires qualified task control and recovery; L has explicit lower demand. Use pattern-specific instructional routes for gaps. Consecutive visitors generally start from D/L alternation; a one-day visitor can take D on any weekday when ready. A symptom/restriction stop is not converted into an L clearance.
equipment_space: UNVERIFIED MODEL: three noncrossing running lanes with separate outside walking returns, target+20m runoff and clear start queues; the reference requires35m beyond the start for15m+20m, plus a separate clear start/waiting area; no20m sprint is prescribed in this exemplar. The standard preparation requires the separately specified15 marked bays. Strength A:5 individual goblet implements. B:5 appropriate benches,5 row dumbbells and5 stable individually appropriate incline supports. C:5 matched pairs of dumbbells and5 mats/targets. Thus20 working dumbbells/implements may be needed simultaneously, plus load choices; names in the equipment catalog do not prove availability. Stage equipment outside all active travel/runoff. Verify actual width, support heights, sightlines and inventory before release.
coaching_flow: Two qualified athletic coaches are assumed. Running: one coach releases three lanes, the other watches target/runoff/returns. Strength: three groups of five rotate A knee, B row/push and C hinge/brace; coach1 owns A, coach2 watches adjacent B/C. Loaded hinge bouts are staggered against B's main loaded-row bouts; only familiar, lower-demand floor control may overlap. If the coach cannot see or safely supervise the active tasks, serialize/reduce work and recalculate instead of assuming another coach.
time_rules: All times include instruction, handling, recovery, water, return travel and transitions. Release times are earliest opportunities. Wait for clear lanes and quality recovery. A4-effort reference is not six because six slots exist; only a documented six-effort standard carryover uses the two extra slots. Compressed work explicitly loses strength sets and any extra sprint carryover, not its rest or runway.
preparation_note: The export below expands the familiar full/compact base for all three ages, preserving concluding hinge/squat checks. Apply only qualified drill levels. The two targeted tasks P1 and P2 follow the base; no extra preparatory circuit is inserted. D/L use the appropriate mastered low-fatigue base; physical symptoms still stop/modify the relevant task.

exercises.name: Start position check
exercises.mapping: ACC-STATIC: setup rehearsal of two-point-static; preparation delivery mapping pending
exercises.set_purpose: The3s check has one purpose: organize familiar foot pressure, projection and trunk control before faster starts; observe readiness without tiring the athlete.
exercises.execution: Gather from the marked bays to the three start queues; use the habitual stagger and still start, arms ready and weight controlled over the base. Hold the selected position briefly, then stand.
exercises.cues: Own the start; stay still until release; push the floor behind you.
exercises.errors: Falling before the signal, an overlong stagger, a tense breath-hold or reaching instead of a controlled lean.
exercises.rationale: Exactly the first targeted task. It informs acceleration setup and the trunk/foot-pressure demands of later squatting without claiming a maximal force stimulus.
exercises.metadata: Methodology: task rehearsal. Tenets: Coordination/Balance. Physiology: movement preparation. Pattern: start posture/brace. Equipment: marked lane.

exercises.name: Progressive short-start rehearsal
exercises.mapping: ACC-STATIC identity; submaximal Prepare & Access use is a proposed delivery override
exercises.set_purpose: Effort1 establishes a comfortable route; effort2 rehearses purposeful intent without reaching the main sprint demand. Both prepare the selected start/run-through and verify clearance.
exercises.execution: Two5m starts from the same stance. Clear10m gradual runoff, exit sideways only into the marked return route and walk back outside active lanes. Coach1 releases; coach2 monitors runway/exit.
exercises.cues: Build the effort; run through the marker; use all the clear runoff.
exercises.errors: Treating rehearsal as a race, stopping at5m, entering another lane or returning against active traffic.
exercises.rationale: Exactly the second targeted task; it builds from the position check into today's actual movement. No extra jump drill is added simply to potentiate.
exercises.metadata: Method: progressive rehearsal. Tenets: Speed/Coordination. Physiology: movement preparation. Pattern: short acceleration. Equipment: lane markers.

exercises.competency: D uses easy then purposeful submaximal running. L uses two easy efforts at the same distance. Every age uses the same short rehearsal because its job is preparation; a person without route competence uses the explicit OR walking orientation instead of being counted as sprint-ready.
exercises.progression: Use main running only after route and mechanics are repeatable. Reduce the intended effort or stop; do not add repetitions to compensate.
exercises.continuity: P1 and prior qualified route → two5m rehearsals → today's E1. These10m are recorded separately from high-intent distance.

exercises.name: Repeatable short acceleration
exercises.mapping: ACC-STATIC:10-yard-sprint / two-point-static / output-two-point-static candidate; current release unverified
exercises.set_purpose: Working efforts1–4, plus efforts5–6 only for the documented standard six-effort carryover, share the primary job: retain and express familiar short acceleration with adequate recovery and a comparable starting record. L efforts1–2 retain a lower-demand route without claiming high-intent output.
exercises.execution: Set a10m target for9–11 and15m for12–14/15–18, each followed by20m clear gradual runoff. Begin from the habitual two-point static start. Accelerate through the target, decelerate gradually beyond it, exit to the outside walking route, and return to the assigned queue.
exercises.cues: Still start; push behind you; finish through, then slow down smoothly.
exercises.errors: Overstriding, rising abruptly, racing a neighbor, braking at the timing line or losing lane/runoff control.
exercises.rationale: The sole primary explosive task keeps the opening comparison clean. Unresisted static starts have less setup than resisted or falling starts and preserve a familiar acceleration anchor. Long shuttles would change the stimulus to repeated braking/fatigue and are not selected.
exercises.metadata: Method: fully recovered quality attempts. Tenets: Speed/Explosiveness. Physiology: rapid force expression. Pattern: acceleration/run-through. Body region: whole body with lower-limb emphasis. Equipment: measured corridor/markers/timing method if available.

exercises.competency: Within every age, D requires an already demonstrated start and controlled runoff. A returning/less-ready athlete uses that age's explicit L dose. An established athlete whose actual productive record is SIX efforts may use six standard-D efforts at the same age distance and load-free task, at19/23/27/31/35/39min; no new distance or intensity increase. Otherwise the written default is four. Compressed D remains four, a stated volume reduction for that six-effort athlete. No catch-up reps.
exercises.progression: Continue only while the familiar action and stopping remain controlled. Rest longer or end the exposure if quality stays below the athlete's normal level; no universal percentage slowdown is invented. Day10 holds the sprint task while a separately qualified knee-load change may be selected.
exercises.continuity: Most recent actual productive and review ACC exposures →4 planned high-intent efforts today (or recorded6-effort standard carryover) →Day10 ACC. Day2 is adjacent JUMP work: use L if consecutive participation/recovery warrants it; its different name does not erase leg load.

exercises.name: Retained knee-pattern strength
exercises.mapping: GOBLET; L/within-age instructional alternative SQUAT-BW; both current release mappings pending
exercises.set_purpose: All working sets provide the lead general force stimulus at a familiar range and effort. The L sets retain controlled knee-pattern practice at lower demand; they are not recorded as loaded squat progression.
exercises.execution: Pick up one appropriate dumbbell under control, hold it near the chest, set a stable base, lower through owned range and stand. Park it safely after each set. The unloaded alternative uses the exact tempo-bodyweight squat with a brief bottom pause.
exercises.cues: Whole foot; sit between your hips; stand without losing your trunk.
exercises.errors: Load drifting away, uncontrolled knees/trunk, bouncing out of depth or grinding the final repetition.
exercises.rationale: Goblet loading is a measurable retained knee anchor with one implement. A box/contact or front-rack variation changes setup and is used only for a documented reason; no novel lift is needed to begin a continuing block.
exercises.metadata: Method: controlled straight sets. Tenets: Strength/Body Control. Physiology: force capacity. Pattern: squat/brace. Regions: legs/trunk. Equipment: one individual dumbbell; no weight for SQUAT-BW.

exercises.competency: Every age first confirms safe handling, controlled range and the intended reserve. A pattern-specific new/less-ready athlete uses that age's explicit L squat dose while qualified parts of the session may stay D. Experienced athletes retain an appropriate known load with the written sets; being older does not require a different lift. If actual prior work differs, log the exact current decision and recalculate rather than claim this template is athlete history.
exercises.progression: Hold load today. At Day10 consider one smallest practical load step only when actual productive knee work was repeatable at the stated range/effort and recovery fits; otherwise hold. Stop/regress lost control, pain or a restriction before forcing repetitions.
exercises.continuity: Prior actual productive knee dose plus latest review →today's written2 or3×6 goblet reference →Day2 smaller knee support; next matching ACC lead is Day10. A light review dose alone does not overwrite productive history.

exercises.name: Supported pulling
exercises.mapping: SUPPORTED-ROW:one-arm-dumbbell-row / bench-supported-dumbbell / capacity-strength candidate; source defaults explicitly overridden
exercises.set_purpose: Each prescribed working set maintains complementary upper-body pulling at controlled effort. They broaden the session without being called a direct sprint drill or borrowing the squat's load progression.
exercises.execution: Support the opposite hand AND knee on a stable bench with the other foot grounded. Pick up one dumbbell, row toward the hip/trunk without rotating, lower under control, change sides in the stated10s and finish both sides before parking the load.
exercises.cues: Quiet trunk; elbow toward hip; lower the weight under control.
exercises.errors: Hand-only standing support under the wrong variant label, twisting, shrugging, dropping the dumbbell or forgetting the second side.
exercises.rationale: Bench support makes the pulling task observable and avoids another unsupported hinge. It is paired with pushing only through scheduled actual recovery; these shoulder/trunk tasks are not assumed noncompeting.

exercises.name: Complementary hip-pattern strength
exercises.set_purpose: The two standard working sets retain a useful hip force/range exposure while knee strength leads. One compressed set preserves a smaller dose. The L hinge is low-demand technical retention, not a loaded RDL result.
exercises.execution: Begin tall with TWO dumbbells close to the thighs, soft knees and an organized trunk. Send hips back within owned hamstring-limited range, return to standing, and park both loads safely. The unloaded alternative crosses arms at the chest and uses the authored bodyweight good-morning hinge.
exercises.cues: Soft knees; hips back; keep the weights close; stand tall.
exercises.errors: Turning it into a squat, chasing floor contact, losing grip/trunk control, bouncing or using one implement while claiming the two-DB variant.
exercises.rationale: A familiar bilateral RDL maintains the hip anchor; its grip and trunk demand is counted alongside rowing and later tumbling. Loaded RDL bouts are staggered against the upper station's demanding bouts so the second coach can prioritize them.

exercises.name: Low-load moving-limb brace practice
exercises.mapping: HEEL-TAP:source66 arms-fixed heel-tap candidate; placement in Strength is a proposed contextual adaptation, not a verified Strength profile
exercises.set_purpose: Each set rehearses trunk organization during controlled alternating leg motion at low fatigue. It fills the explicit brace role without claiming it adds another heavy strength stimulus.
exercises.execution: Lie on a stable mat, arms vertical and still, hips/knees in comfortable tabletop. Lower one bent leg to a declared light heel target, return to tabletop, then alternate. Use comfortable breathing and a shorter target range before forcing floor contact.
exercises.cues: Arms still; light heel; quiet trunk; return before switching.
exercises.errors: Moving the opposite arm, sliding the heel, arching, holding the breath, confusing eight total taps with eight pairs or forcing a low target.
exercises.rationale: This small moving-limb control task adds little grip demand after the hinge and helps preserve shoulder/wrist capacity for tumbling. A loaded carry would add grip and travel constraints already present elsewhere; it is not required to fill the brace role today.
exercises.metadata: Method: low-load control practice. Tenets: Body Control/Coordination. Physiology: trunk/pelvis control. Pattern: supine brace with alternating hip motion. Regions: trunk/hip. Equipment: mat, declared padding target if needed.

standard_D.notes: One rep is ONE heel contact and return, not a left/right pair. Use padding as an elevated heel target if needed while preserving light contact. This is proposed complementary brace practice inside Strength; the inspected source has only a Prepare & Access profile.

timing_narrative:
**Targets (same180s allocation in both bookings):** first40s includes15s moving from bays to assigned queues,10s briefing and three5s observation waves (one3s position hold per athlete, one five-athlete group at a time). The next140s uses five waves per lane at offsets0/12/24/36/48s, then60/72/84/96/108s for the second5m rehearsal (purposeful D/easy L). Each wave has a12s work/runoff-clearance budget; returning athletes use the outside route. The final wave clears by120s and has20s to walk back, so return time fits the140s allocation. At least45s remains after an effort before the same athlete's next start. If clearance/return cannot fit, the layout/dose must be revised, not overlapped.

**Standard running:**15–19min briefing, route/measurement check and readiness. Four reference rounds begin19,23,27,31min, each with five three-athlete waves at0/25/50/75/100s. Each runner has an8s work budget,20s combined work/runoff-clearance budget and40s return budget, all within the4min individual start interval. The last reference wave starts32:40 and can be back by33:40. Record comparable observations, give concise feedback and recover in unused time. Only athletes with a documented6-effort productive dose also use35/39min rounds; the final wave at40:40 is back by41:40.41:40–45min accommodates final recording, water and strength transfer. Keep repetitions per side, external loads, tempo and brace practice separate rather than treating all sets as equivalent fatigue. Alternatives replace their designated set allocation. age_scaling_policy.equal_dose_reason: Short low-effort preparation is not age-based overload. Explicit equal doses across ages are deliberate; task skill, body size, comfortable range and current readiness decide the variant.
age_scaling_policy.readiness_independent_of_age: Experienced younger athletes may use qualified familiar actions; unfamiliar older athletes use instruction. Age never grants flight, rapid descent, floor support, loaded patterns or cue response.

layout_and_timing_assumptions.layout: Three columns of five distinct 3 m × 3 m personal bays: 15 independent working spaces. Five athletes share a lane assignment, never an overlapping crawl corridor.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.additional_space: Unobstructed peripheral coach circulation/access/egress and separately verified start, runoff and return corridors are additional to the 9 m × 15 m bay rectangle. The marked rectangle is not the total facility footprint.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.travel: Standing paths remain in personal bays. Short forward passes are at most 1.6 m; backward/lateral spans 1 m or less except 1.5 m carioca. Individually check full hand-walk/plank footprint before use.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.orientation: All bays face one end. Complete a pass and stop before ordinary walking return within that same bay. No crossing between athletes or concurrent opposite-direction traffic inside a bay.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.coaches: Familiar shared practice: one coach scans A/B and one scans B/C with clear oblique views. Three-wave teaching/checks: both coaches watch one active lane and split five athletes 2/3; other lanes stand. Clear views of all active feet/trunks are required.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.wave_handover: The active lane finishes standing, then the next lane starts on cue. The 2-second change (3 seconds for floor teaching) is a cue change, not relocation. Athletes stay in their own bays.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.equipment: Flat markers, bottles outside active rectangles, clean dry nonslip surface. No partner support, unstable props or unverified anchor is assumed.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.setup_before_clock: Mark/inspect space before class. Readiness/restriction information must be available. First demonstration includes stop cue and immediate comfort check. Unknown restrictions or inability to follow safe directions require individual resolution, never assumed clearance.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.clock_definition: Row time = demonstration + waves × individual execution envelope + explicit wave handovers + reset/transition. The individual envelope includes stated steps, pauses and returns. Shared practice means separate bays, not 15 times one athlete dose.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.tempo_rule: Execution envelopes are estimates for the stated variant, not speed commands. If safe learning/movement needs longer, use contingency, remove optional work or revise the booking. Never rush to validate arithmetic.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.bay_to_target_transition: Base ends at 12:00 full or 7:00 compact with athletes standing in bays. Reserve exactly 180 seconds for exactly two parent-owned target tasks. The parent exemplar defines the split and charges bay-to-start gathering, demonstrations, observed holds, rehearsal, exit and return within those 180 seconds. Use the parent-defined allocation; do not double-charge gathering or hide it before the base ends.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.physical_validation_status: UNVERIFIED: measured space, body fit, sightlines, surface, shared-floor schedule and target corridors have not been observed. Arithmetic does not certify physical feasibility.

teaching_and_competency_policy.full_familiar: Sixteen ordered slots with reminder demonstrations only. SP-11/SP-12 explicitly repeat mastered A-March because exact B/C identities are unverified.
teaching_and_competency_policy.compact_familiar: Eleven slots in original relative order. Omit SP-04, SP-10, SP-11, SP-12, SP-14. Retain floor purpose through the declared stationary-bear modification; hinge and squat remain last.
teaching_and_competency_policy.or01_full: Eleven recognizable slots in 12 minutes. Easy march replaces jog; optional crossing/flight/B/C complexity is omitted; lunges lose rotation/depth; floor flow becomes knees-down rock-backs; descent is slow; basic march/foot-roll precede observed hinge and partial squat-to-stand. After the easy raise, all actions are demonstrated and observed in three five-athlete waves.
teaching_and_competency_policy.or01_compact: Same eleven recognizable slots in 7 minutes. Basic walking/stepping/foot-roll can follow the coach in separate bays. Lunge, floor, slow drop, hinge and partial squat remain serialized in three observed five-athlete waves. One hinge and one squat cycle are readiness observations; qualification belongs to subsequent instructional work.
deferred_complexity: Traveling bear crawl and new complete plank/downward-dog flow
Full toe/ankle contact and overhead squat-to-stand range when unavailable
teaching_and_competency_policy.what_deferred_means: Practice the simpler named component in its original place; log performed variant and unfilled demand. Teach additional complexity in a relevant later instructional module. Do not silently pass it, substitute a generic unrelated warm-up or add teaching outside the clock.
teaching_and_competency_policy.partial_competency: Existing evidence can support a familiar variation, independently of age. Preparation completion does not unlock a main family: no-flight lowering is not landing, marching is not running, rock-back is not tumbling, and no throw/cue gate is tested here.
teaching_and_competency_policy.correction_limit: Use visible contingency for actual slower movement or brief corrective repeat and record time/dose/contacts. If essential teaching remains incomplete, mark profile/session REVISE and use the 12-minute instructional base or a justified booking adjustment. Never consume the reserved target time or speed up movement.
teaching_and_competency_policy.optional_reduction_order: For familiar full, remove SP-12 then SP-11, then SP-04/SP-10/SP-14 as readiness/purpose permits. Record omissions and revised clock. Compact/OR already omit these; beyond contingency, further necessary omissions require explicit review rather than an unqualified complete-base claim.

records.name: Backpedal
records.purpose: Rehearse controlled backward travel and orientation.

card_mapping_status.limit: A related backpedal-to-sprint identity is not this slow preparation task.

records.setup: Face the same end of the room. Mark 1 m behind the start; two short backward steps reach it, then two forward walking steps return. No turn or crossing.
cues: Short steps under you; look forward.
Check the clear space behind you before moving.
common_errors: Long reaching steps and backward lean.
stop_rules: Stop for obstacle, balance loss or pain; use ordinary walking return only when clear.

competency_rule.observe: Controls both backward steps and forward return with balance and stop-cue response.
competency_rule.pass_scope: Preparation observation only. A completed repetition does not grant a main-family, loaded-strength, flight, throwing, cue-response or tumbling qualification.
competency_rule.record: Log selected profile, actual variant/dose, comfort, response to cue, omissions and not-observed actions. No actual results are invented.

records.name: Inchworm → plank → bear crawl → downward dog (ordered slot)
records.purpose: Prepare shoulder/wrist support, trunk control, hip movement and floor transitions with low fatigue.

verified_local_names: Inchworm → plank → bear crawl → downward dog
Inchworm to World’s Greatest Stretch (related legacy flow)
card_mapping_status.limit: Exact composite not established. Stationary limb unloads explicitly replace traveling bear crawl for 15-bay delivery. Knees-down rock-backs are a declared partial-purpose regression, not an exact approved composite. The proposed stationary substitution is specifically four separately mastered single-limb lifts with full replants, not an unspecified weight shift or contralateral crawl.

records.setup: One athlete per dry nonslip 3 m × 3 m bay. Entire floor footprint fits before use. No shared slow-crawl lane or following crawler. Coach checks hand/knee comfort before support. Familiar bear support uses one limb at a time: left hand, right hand, left foot, right foot. A lift means the whole selected hand or foot briefly clears the floor by about 1–2 cm; it is not merely a weight shift. Fully replant and settle before the next limb.
cues: Hands comfortable; breathe with controlled trunk.
Quiet unhurried transitions; soft knees in downward dog.
Keep the trunk quiet; lift one contact only, then fully replant before the next.
Do not lift opposite hand and foot together.
common_errors: Forced straight knees or shoulder range.
Starting the next lift before the previous contact is fully replanted.
Rotating or sagging the trunk to clear the limb.
stop_rules: Stop for wrist/shoulder pain, slipping, trunk-control loss or inadequate footprint.
Use contingency or record incomplete rather than rushing floor entry.

Omit the familiar bear-lift component if any single-limb lift/replant has not already been mastered; use the entire named instructional floor profile and its coaching clock, or record incomplete purpose. No new bear-lift teaching is assumed inside the familiar reminder.

competency_rule.observe: Comfortable actual support and floor entry/exit. Rock-back does not pass plank/bear or tumbling support. For familiar bear lifts, each selected contact clears briefly, fully replants, and the trunk remains quiet before the next lift.
competency_rule.pass_scope: Preparation observation only. A completed repetition does not grant a main-family, loaded-strength, flight, throwing, cue-response or tumbling qualification.
competency_rule.record: Log selected profile, actual variant/dose, comfort, response to cue, omissions and not-observed actions. No actual results are invented.

records.setup: Two 1.6 m forward passes inside the bay. Return only after completing a pass. First visit stays in place.
cues: Stand over the support foot; opposite arm and leg.
Place the foot close beneath you.
stop_rules: Stop for balance, comfort or rhythm failure; use basic walking march with same or smaller dose, logged as changed variant.

competency_rule.observe: Controlled actual support/exchange; neither march variant proves sprint competence.

competency_rule.record: Log selected profile, actual variant/dose, comfort, response to cue, omissions and not-observed actions. No actual results are invented.

records.setup: Tiny forward steps within 1 m; walk back after the pass. First visit stays in place with both feet available for balance.

stop_rules: Stop for foot/ankle discomfort, uncontrolled impact or lost rhythm; use no-flight option only when comfortable.

records.purpose: Provide a small already qualified bilateral elastic rehearsal.

card_mapping_status.limit: Source 48, stationary-bilateral-low-amplitude-ankle-pogo. Current publication and live delivery eligibility remain unverified.

records.setup: Center of clear bay with no implement; only already qualified low bilateral rebounds.
cues: Small quiet rebounds under you.
Stop at six and settle.
stop_rules: Stop for pain, increasing noise, asymmetry, height escalation or lost position; no makeup contacts.

competency_rule.observe: Owns familiar small rebound/stop; this is not permission for extra later impacts.
competency_rule.pass_scope: Preparation observation only. A completed repetition does not grant a main-family, loaded-strength, flight, throwing, cue-response or tumbling qualification.

full.variant: Stationary low-amplitude bilateral ankle pogo
full.tempo: About one low rebound per second; contact quality takes priority over cadence.
full.effort: Easy and conversational; no maximal speed, height, stretch or fatigue target.

rest.within_set: Only the pauses, resets and walking returns explicitly included in execution_segments.
rest.after_set: Use the row transition and next demonstration. Waiting waves add no repetitions. Extra required rest uses visible contingency, then an explicit reduction/revision.

full.other_contact_accounting: Six bilateral landing events, six per foot: event count 6, foot-contact count 12.
full.prerequisite: Previously passed comfortable low bilateral rebound and stop; current total impact budget permits it.
full.count_definition: One bilateral rebound and landing is one event involving both feet; do not double the event count when summing feet.

count_reconciliation.calculation: 6 bilateral landing events × 2 feet = 12 landing foot contacts (6 each foot), not 12 rebound repetitions.
count_reconciliation.partial_cycle_rule: A fraction in conversion arithmetic is not an accepted partial repetition. Record completed whole cycles/actions/sequences actually performed.

contact_accounting.foot_contact_unit: One foot contacting the surface; bilateral landing contributes two foot contacts.

contact_accounting.unknown_count_rule: Null means not predetermined or not a total-contact prescription; never coerce it to zero. A zero flight count does not mean zero standing/support/step contacts.

records.purpose: Observe knee/hip/trunk organization through a comfortable sequence.

card_mapping_status.limit: Source 62 is review state. Familiar prescription follows candidate variant sequential-bilateral-reach-squat-to-stand: standing hinge/contact, comfortable squat, one controlled overhead reach per assigned side, stand/reset. Assigned order is left then right. Current exact dose/profile eligibility remains unverified. The OR thigh-supported partial version remains an explicitly different modification pending variant review.

records.setup: Same three five-athlete observation waves. Comfortable stance/reachable contact points; no forced toe touch or depth. Coaches see feet and trunk. Familiar source-linked sequence assigns LEFT reach and return, then RIGHT reach and return while the opposite hand maintains its comfortable toe/ankle contact; stand only after both reaches. Each reach stays in controlled comfortable range.
cues: Use comfortable range and a stable foot.
Reach without forced rib flare; stand smoothly.
Left reach and return, right reach and return, then stand; do not skip a side.
common_errors: Counting one reach as completion of the familiar sequential-bilateral cycle.
stop_rules: Stop for pain or uncontrolled balance/trunk; use declared partial sequence if comfortable. Longer teaching uses contingency or records incomplete.

competency_rule.record: Log selected profile, actual variant/dose, comfort, response to cue, omissions and not-observed actions. No actual results are invented.

workload_and_tumbling_interface.purpose: Finish warm and organized, not tired. Effort about 2/10 and conversational; this is not overload or conditioning.
workload_and_tumbling_interface.full_flight: Four unilateral A-Skip hop landings and six bilateral pogo landing events are explicitly prescribed in the familiar full profile. Timed easy jog and ankling also carry impact; their actual flight/contact detail is recorded instead of fabricated.
workload_and_tumbling_interface.compact_flight: A-Skip/pogo are omitted, but easy jog still has impact and ankling actual contacts remain in the record. Compressed is not automatically impact-free.
workload_and_tumbling_interface.or01_flight: No intentional flight in the first-visit profiles; no landing gate is thereby passed.
workload_and_tumbling_interface.upper_body: Familiar floor work includes a 4-second high plank, brief bear-position support/unloads and downward-dog access. Count wrist/shoulder/trunk demand alongside throwing, pressing, bracing and separate tumbling. Rock-back support is still support.
workload_and_tumbling_interface.tumbling: The separate 30-minute tumbling/Body Control allocation remains unprescribed here. Share actual comfort, support/impact exposure and observations with its coach. Its later load and staffing remain unverified.
